reference.title: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you drive the hips up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.8 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbell, a 2 s squeeze, then a barbell or single-leg hip thrust. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Upper back on the bench edge, feet flat about hip width, one dumbbell across the hip crease held at both ends.
Breathe out and drive through the heels to lift the hips.
Hips level with the shoulders and knees, shins vertical, chin tucked. Squeeze.
Breathe in and lower the hips toward the floor under control.
Keep the dumbbell steady on the hips and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to get higher
mistakes.fix: Stop when the trunk is level; ribs down, chin tucked.

mistakes.mistake: Feet too far out or too close
mistakes.fix: Place the feet so the shins are vertical at the top.
Hold it at both ends on the hip crease.
Pivot on the shoulder blades; the bench edge stays under the same spot.

kinematics.norm: Knee-height bench, about 40-45 cm (common setup; clinical opinion)
Hip reaches neutral at the top, trunk level with the floor (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees at the top (shins vertical) (common coaching); foot position changes muscle use (Collazo García 2020)
Level at the top; the trunk pivots on the shoulder blades (clinical opinion)
Rests across the hip crease, held at both ends (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up, a short pause, about 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #474212, Dumbbell Hip Thrust, video (movement reference)

Contreras, Vigotsky, Schoenfeld, Beardsley & Cronin 2015, a comparison of gluteus maximus, biceps femoris and vastus lateralis EMG in the back squat and barbell hip thrust (J Appl Biomech 31(6):452-458)
Krause Neto, Soares, Vieira et al. 2020, gluteus maximus activation during common strength and hypertrophy exercises: a systematic review (J Sports Sci Med 19(1):195-203)
Collazo García, Rueda, Suárez Luginick & Navarro 2020, differences in the electromyographic activity of lower-body muscles in hip thrust variations (J Strength Cond Res 34(9):2449-2455)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Set the bench against a wall so it cannot slide.
Pad the dumbbell with a towel if it presses on the hip bones.
modify: Low back discomfort: lift less high and brace first.
Neck discomfort: keep the chin tucked and the head moving with the trunk.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Main hip extensor. The barbell hip thrust gave about twice the mean upper and lower gluteus maximus EMG of the back squat (69.5% vs 29.4% and 86.8% vs 45.4% MVIC; Contreras 2015). Hip thrust variations were among the highest gluteus maximus exercises in a systematic review (Krause Neto 2020).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Main hip extensor. The barbell hip thrust gave about twice the mean upper and lower gluteus maximus EMG of the back squat (69.5% vs 29.4% and 86.8% vs 45.4% MVIC; Contreras 2015). Hip thrust variations were among the highest gluteus maximus exercises in a systematic review (Krause Neto 2020).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; biceps femoris EMG was higher in the hip thrust than in the back squat (40.8% vs 14.9% MVIC; Contreras 2015). Moving the feet farther out changes the pattern (Collazo García 2020).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension; biceps femoris EMG was higher in the hip thrust than in the back squat (40.8% vs 14.9% MVIC; Contreras 2015). Moving the feet farther out changes the pattern (Collazo García 2020).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Hold the knees at about 90 degrees and press the feet into the floor; vastus lateralis EMG was similar to the back squat (Contreras 2015).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Hold the knees at about 90 degrees and press the feet into the floor; vastus lateralis EMG was similar to the back squat (Contreras 2015).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and keeps the knees in line (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and keeps the knees in line (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knees from caving in (clinical opinion); its activity did not change across hip thrust variations (Collazo García 2020).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knees from caving in (clinical opinion); its activity did not change across hip thrust variations (Collazo García 2020).
muscleNotes.core: Holds the ribs down so the lift comes from the hips, not the low back.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk straight; they should not take over by arching (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk straight; they should not take over by arching (clinical opinion).
